summary: Material change since the prior snapshot: the scheduled Oman meeting between Iran and Gulf Arab states on reopening the Strait of Hormuz was postponed, removing a near-term diplomatic de-escalation catalyst while Saudi bypass-pipeline and maritime risks remain active. Brent rose to about $107.84/bbl and WTI to about $102.85/bbl in early September 14 Asian trade. Separately, repeated Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries have reduced fuel production, prompted a public U.S. request for Ukraine to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure, and add a second refined-product supply shock. No new U.S., Taiwan or China official macro release was identified since the prior snapshot.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: The risk mix remains adverse for Taiwan equities: near-5% U.S. long yields, an 86% Reuters-reported market probability of a September Fed hike, renewed oil gains above $100, persistent Hormuz/Bab el-Mandeb disruption and a separate Russia-Ukraine refined-product shock all pressure valuation, freight, imported inflation and margins. Strong AI/HPC export demand remains the main offset.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Reuters market probabilities, intraday oil observations and conflict-related supply estimates are semantic evidence only and must not overwrite deterministic macro series.

key_drivers.name: Hormuz diplomacy postponed as oil reprices higher
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported that the scheduled Oman meeting between Iran and Gulf Arab states on reopening the Strait of Hormuz was postponed. Brent was about $107.84/bbl and WTI about $102.85/bbl in early September 14 Asian trade.
key_drivers.interpretation: A near-term diplomatic de-escalation catalyst has weakened while physical supply and shipping constraints remain active, raising persistence risk for imported energy inflation and freight costs.

key_drivers.name: Russia-Ukraine refinery attacks add a refined-product shock
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported repeated Ukrainian long-range drone strikes have reduced Russian fuel production. President Trump urged Ukraine to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure, while Russia has downgraded its 2026 oil-output forecast and fuel-export outlook because of the war.
key_drivers.interpretation: This creates a second energy channel, focused on diesel/refining, which can reinforce freight, inflation and rate pressure independently of Middle East crude disruptions.

key_drivers.name: U.S. August CPI remains a hawkish-rate input
key_drivers.observed: Headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y; core CPI rose 0.3% m/m and 2.4% y/y.
key_drivers.interpretation: Reuters reported markets pricing an 86% chance of a 25 bp Fed hike on September 16; this is a market-implied probability, not an official Fed forecast.

key_risks: A sustained U.S. 10Y yield near 5% and a possible renewed Fed hiking cycle can compress long-duration semiconductor and AI-hardware valuation multiples.
Postponed Hormuz diplomacy, attacks on Gulf shipping and the Saudi East-West Pipeline outage increase the probability of persistent delivered-energy, freight and insurance-cost pressure.
Russia-Ukraine attacks on refinery infrastructure add a refined-product/diesel shock that can raise trucking, shipping and industrial logistics costs even if crude supply stabilizes.
Taiwan's strong AI/HPC export cycle offsets but does not eliminate energy, FX, rates and global-demand risks.
DXY, VIX, copper and the latest USD/TWD close remain stale in this semantic snapshot because no sufficiently authoritative newer value was incorporated.

policy_tone.fed: Hawkish risk is elevated after August CPI. Reuters reported markets pricing an 86% chance of a 25 bp hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting; no new official FOMC action has occurred yet.
policy_tone.taiwan_central_bank: No new decision. Imported-energy inflation, U.S. yields and FX pressures remain important ahead of the September 17 meeting.
policy_tone.global: Energy-security risk remains inflationary and growth-negative. Postponed Gulf-Iran diplomacy and Russia-Ukraine refinery disruptions broaden the energy shock from crude/chokepoints to refined products.
